paragraphs: BIOSCAN-1M provides a curated collection of one million insect images to support image-based biodiversity assessment. Each record combines expert taxonomic classification with genetic information: a raw nucleotide barcode sequence and a barcode index number. The index numbers serve as genetic proxies for species classification, connecting visual records with another source of biological information.

The dataset presents classification challenges that arise from the organisms themselves. Its classes follow a long-tailed distribution, so some categories are much more common than others. Labels also form a hierarchy, with increasingly fine distinctions at lower taxonomic levels. A classifier therefore faces both unequal representation and the need to distinguish closely related categories.

The paper introduces this resource and implements and analyzes a baseline classifier to explore the classification task. Its contribution is a foundation for developing and studying taxonomic recognition systems. Progress on that task could support BIOSCAN’s broader aim of a comprehensive global biodiversity survey, while also providing machine learning research with a biologically grounded classification problem.
neurips-2023-a-step-towards-worldwide-bi.tldr: BIOSCAN-1M pairs a million expert-labeled insect images with genetic information to support biodiversity assessment and challenging classification research.

paragraphs: The paper investigates why neural networks often trail tree-based methods on tabular data. Its hypothesis is that heterogeneous table columns produce irregular relationships between inputs and targets, while neural networks tend to learn smoother functions. Spectral analysis supports the observation that target functions in tabular datasets often have substantial irregularity.

Transformations such as scaling or ranking can make these relationships smoother and improve prediction. However, they can also discard information or make optimization harder, requiring careful tuning for individual features. The authors instead introduce a network layer that encourages low-frequency representations of input features. This gives the network a representation space in which the target function is more regular.

The proposed layer adds less computational complexity than a fully connected layer. Across 14 tabular datasets, the authors report significant performance improvements and faster convergence. These findings support frequency reduction as a useful learning preference for the evaluated tasks, while the proposed explanation for the broader gap between neural networks and trees remains a hypothesis.
neurips-2023-an-inductive-bias-for-tabul.tldr: A lightweight layer encourages smoother feature representations and improves neural network performance and convergence on 14 tabular datasets.

paragraphs: BiMatting addresses the computational demands of video matting on devices with limited resources. Binarization reduces memory and computation through one-bit parameters and bitwise operations, but applying it directly to a matting model can damage quality. The authors identify two empirical problems: the encoder loses substantial representational ability, and the decoder performs many redundant computations.

The method changes both parts of the model to address these distinct bottlenecks. Its binarized encoder blocks use shrinkable and densely connected topologies to improve the representations they extract. In the decoder, sparsifying binarized units reduces computation that contributes little information. The design therefore combines representation improvements with selective reductions in decoding work.

Experiments show substantial gains over other binarized video matting models, including leading binarization methods. The authors also report visual quality comparable to the full-precision counterpart, alongside computation and storage savings of 12.4 times and 21.6 times, respectively. These results indicate that architecture changes can help preserve useful visual quality while realizing the resource benefits of binarization.
neurips-2023-bimatting-efficient-video-m.tldr: BiMatting redesigns a binarized video matting encoder and decoder to retain visual quality while sharply reducing computation and storage.

paragraphs: Causal discovery becomes difficult when measurements arrive less frequently than causal effects occur. Events at unobserved time steps act as hidden variables, potentially distorting the relationships seen in the recorded series. The paper addresses this subsampling problem with an algorithm intended to recover the entire causal structure without imposing a parametric form on the relationships.

The central observation uses the temporal organization of the data. A hidden variable at an unmeasured time has an observed proxy in the form of that same variable at a later, measured time. The authors use these proxies to remove bias associated with the hidden variables. This leads to a constraint-based causal discovery procedure rather than one restricted to linear relationships.

The paper establishes full causal identification for its proposed approach and reports synthetic and real-world experiments reflecting its theoretical advantages. Identification matters because the goal is to distinguish the underlying causal structure, beyond simply finding associations in the sampled observations. The contribution links that goal to information supplied by later observations of otherwise hidden variables.
neurips-2023-causal-discovery-from-subsa.tldr: A nonparametric causal discovery algorithm uses later observations as proxies for hidden intermediate variables in subsampled time series.

paragraphs: Chameleon tackles reasoning tasks by giving a language model access to complementary modules. Its motivation is that answering some questions requires current external information, visual processing, or precise computation. The system combines language models with tools including vision models, search engines, Python functions, and heuristic modules.

An LLM-based planner assembles these components into a sequence of operations that produces the final response. In this sense, the system synthesizes a program for each task: it selects tools and composes their use. This approach matters because a complex question can require several kinds of processing that are supplied by different modules.

The authors evaluate Chameleon on ScienceQA and TabMWP. With GPT-4, it achieves 86.54% overall accuracy on ScienceQA and 98.78% on TabMWP, improving the reported comparison results. Their analysis also finds that the GPT-4 planner makes more consistent and rational tool selections than a ChatGPT-powered planner by inferring potential constraints from instructions. The findings support both modular reasoning and the importance of the planner choosing the modules.
neurips-2023-chameleon-plug-and-play-com.tldr: Chameleon uses an LLM planner to compose external tools into reasoning programs, improving results on ScienceQA and TabMWP.

paragraphs: Individual preference stability asks whether each point is reasonably well served by its assigned cluster. Specifically, its average distance to its own cluster must be at most a factor alpha times its average distance to any alternative cluster. A smaller factor gives a stronger guarantee for every point, connecting clustering quality with individual preferences.

Determining whether a dataset admits a clustering with factor one is NP-hard. Before this work, the available general guarantee allowed a factor growing linearly with the number of points. The paper proves that a constant-factor stable clustering always exists in general metric spaces and provides an efficient algorithm to construct one.

This changes the guarantee from one that weakens with dataset size to one bounded by a constant. It does not claim to efficiently solve exact factor-one stability. The authors also extend the objective beyond average distances, considering maximum and minimum distances within and between clusters, and provide efficient, nearly optimal algorithms for those variants.
neurips-2023-constant-approximation-for-.tldr: The paper proves that constant-factor individually stable clusterings exist in general metric spaces and gives an efficient construction algorithm.

paragraphs: Text rationalization extracts understandable pieces of an input to explain a model’s prediction. A common objective selects text that carries strong information about the target label. The paper argues that this can favor spurious features, because a feature may correlate with the label or its causal explanation without being part of that explanation.

The proposed Minimum Conditional Dependence criterion asks a different question: after accounting for the selected rationale, how much dependence remains between the omitted text and the label? Its basis is the authors’ finding that the causal rationale d-separates non-causal features from the target. Under that causal relationship, minimizing the remaining dependence compels the selection of all causes of the label.

The authors use KL-divergence as a practical dependence measure to evaluate this criterion. Experiments report F1 improvements of up to 13.7% over earlier leading methods based on maximum mutual information. The contribution is an explanation objective that evaluates what relevant dependence remains outside a rationale, giving a causal motivation for how text should be selected.
neurips-2023-d-separation-for-causal-sel.tldr: A causal rationale criterion selects text by minimizing the label dependence that remains in omitted text after conditioning on the rationale.

paragraphs: The paper studies private range counting, such as estimating how many data points lie inside a query ball. Existing approaches face a tradeoff: some have additive errors that grow as a fixed polynomial of dataset size, while others obtain polylogarithmic additive errors at the cost of exponential dependence on dimension.

The authors work with a relaxed boundary. A query for points within radius r may also count points within a larger radius cr, where c exceeds one. Their efficient algorithm has an additive error that can be an arbitrarily small power of dataset size, depending on the permitted boundary fuzziness, together with a multiplicative error of 1 + o(1).

Crucially, the amount of privacy noise has no dependence on dimension. This avoids the dimension-sensitive noise problem while accepting both boundary ambiguity and the stated approximation errors. The algorithm achieves this tradeoff through a new variant and use of locality-sensitive hashing. Its contribution is a different balance among privacy, counting accuracy, and boundary precision in high-dimensional data.
neurips-2023-differentially-private-appr.tldr: A private approximate counting algorithm trades boundary precision for small errors while keeping added noise independent of dimension.

paragraphs: Dual pseudo training connects semi-supervised classification with conditional image generation. The aim is to make both tasks work better when only a few examples have labels. A classifier supplies predicted labels for training a generative model, and the resulting generated images then provide additional training material for the classifier.

The strategy has three stages. First, a classifier learns from partially labeled data and assigns pseudo-labels. Second, a conditional diffusion model learns using those labels and generates pseudo images. Third, the classifier is retrained on a mixture of real and generated images. The two kinds of model therefore contribute different forms of additional supervision.

The authors report leading generation and classification results across the evaluated settings. On ImageNet at 256 by 256 resolution, generation reaches FID scores of 3.08 and 2.52 with one and two labels per class. Classification reaches top-1 accuracies of 59.0%, 69.5%, and 74.4% with one, two, and five labels per class. These results demonstrate that generated-image augmentation can remain useful under extremely limited labeling.
neurips-2023-diffusion-models-and-semi-s.tldr: Dual pseudo training lets a semi-supervised classifier and a diffusion generator improve each other through predicted labels and generated images.

paragraphs: Bayesian optimization searches efficiently for good settings of an expensive objective. In practice, the setting requested may differ from the one actually evaluated because of execution noise, machining errors, or changing context. AIRBO addresses this problem by seeking an optimum that performs consistently well when its inputs are uncertain.

The method models uncertain inputs as distributions, accommodating arbitrary distributional forms. It equips a Gaussian process with Maximum Mean Discrepancy, allowing the model to account directly for these uncertain inputs. A Nyström approximation accelerates posterior inference, addressing the computational burden of using this representation during optimization.

The authors establish a theoretical regret bound that accounts for error in estimating Maximum Mean Discrepancy. They also report experiments on synthetic functions and real problems showing that AIRBO handles varied input uncertainties and achieves state-of-the-art performance. The contribution combines a flexible representation of input randomness with faster inference and an analysis that explicitly includes estimation error, supporting optimization for reliable performance under the evaluated uncertainties.
neurips-2023-efficient-robust-bayesian-o.tldr: AIRBO models uncertain inputs as distributions to search efficiently for settings that perform consistently despite input randomness.

paragraphs: Few-shot prompting lets a language model learn a task from input-output examples included in its prompt. Its performance can change substantially with the examples chosen, their order, and the prompt format. This paper studies prompt construction through predictive bias: whether a fixed prompt skews the model’s predictions with respect to labels or specified attributes.

The authors introduce a metric for this bias and empirically find that highly biased prompts produce unsatisfactory predictions in their investigation. They then use that observation to guide a search for a near-optimal prompt. The search builds on a greedy strategy, making predictive bias a concrete signal for prompt selection.

Experiments across downstream tasks and mainstream models, including GPT-3, show improved in-context learning performance. The method also gives an interpretable reason for selecting one prompt over another through its measured predictive bias. The reported connection between bias and poor quality is empirical; the contribution is a practical selection strategy supported by those observations and the resulting task evaluations.
neurips-2023-fairness-guided-few-shot-pr.tldr: A predictive-bias metric guides greedy prompt selection to improve few-shot language-model performance.

paragraphs: Large pretrained models can perform well with very little downstream data, but adapting them introduces a tension. Fine-tuning may improve task performance while weakening generalization under distribution shift. With only a few training examples, the model is also especially susceptible to overfitting, making it difficult to preserve the benefits of pretraining.

FD-Align introduces a fine-tuning approach centered on maintaining consistency in spurious features across adaptation. Its stated goal is to strengthen generalizability by constraining how these features change during fine-tuning. This differs in emphasis from approaches that concentrate on adjusting the classification head or adding extra structure to the pretrained model.

The authors report extensive experiments supporting the method on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution tasks. They also find that the resulting fine-tuned model can be combined with existing methods for further performance improvements. The findings support feature consistency as a useful consideration when adapting pretrained models from few examples, particularly when performance must carry beyond the distribution used for adaptation.
neurips-2023-fd-align-feature-discrimina.tldr: FD-Align preserves spurious-feature consistency during few-shot fine-tuning to improve generalization on in-distribution and shifted tasks.

paragraphs: Depth-limited search in imperfect-information games often depends on constructing a subgame from public information and players’ beliefs. This requires enumerating or generating the possible histories at the subgame’s root. Although such computations can be straightforward in games such as poker, they may become a substantial obstacle in more complex settings.

The paper formalizes and analyzes this history-filtering problem. It shows that constructing even a single root history is generally intractable, then establishes a necessary and sufficient condition for efficient enumeration. This identifies a computational requirement behind search methods whose effectiveness depends on subgame decomposition.

The authors also propose a Markov Chain Monte Carlo algorithm for generating histories in trick-taking card games, where full enumeration is often too expensive. Experiments in Oh Hell demonstrate improved scalability. Together, the theoretical analysis and generation method clarify when histories can be obtained efficiently and provide a practical approach for a domain in which listing all possibilities can obstruct otherwise useful search.
neurips-2023-history-filtering-in-imperf.tldr: The paper characterizes the difficulty of constructing subgame histories and introduces scalable sampling for trick-taking card games.

paragraphs: HyenaDNA is a genomic foundation model designed to process long DNA sequences while retaining individual nucleotide resolution. Earlier attention-based genomic models faced short context windows because attention scales quadratically with sequence length. Grouping nucleotides into larger tokens also loses the single-character resolution relevant to subtle genetic variation.

The model uses Hyena’s implicit convolutions and is pretrained on the human reference genome. It supports contexts of up to one million nucleotide tokens, with global context available at every layer and subquadratic scaling. The authors report context increases of up to 500 times and training up to 160 times faster than Transformers. They also explore in-context adaptation to new genomic tasks without changing pretrained weights.

After fine-tuning, HyenaDNA reaches state-of-the-art results on 12 of 18 Nucleotide Transformer datasets using substantially fewer parameters and less pretraining data. It also surpasses prior best results on seven of eight GenomicBenchmarks datasets, with an average gain of ten accuracy points. These evaluations support combining long context with nucleotide-level detail for genomic modeling.
neurips-2023-hyenadna-long-range-genomic.tldr: HyenaDNA models up to one million individual nucleotides efficiently and achieves strong results across genomic benchmarks.

paragraphs: A conditional generator takes an input and a random seed, then produces a sample appropriate to that input. The paper asks how to learn such a generator so that the joint distribution of inputs and generated outputs is close to the true joint distribution in total variation. This is a distributional learning objective rather than simply predicting one output.

The authors provide a learning result for a single-layer ReLU conditional generator from paired input-output samples. A central feature is that the guarantee does not require assumptions on the distribution of inputs. They establish this absence of input-distribution assumptions in their model for both linear regression and single-layer ReLU networks.

That property also enables a conditional extension to deeper generative models. If the learner can access a deep model’s internal activations, it can apply the one-layer guarantee progressively and learn the deep model with a near-linear number of samples. Access to those activations is essential to the stated extension: the result connects layerwise guarantees under that access condition.
neurips-2023-learning-a-1-layer-conditio.tldr: The paper learns single-layer conditional generators in total variation without assumptions on the input distribution, with a conditional extension to deep models.

paragraphs: Model Shapley addresses how to value pretrained models in an AI marketplace when buyers or evaluators can query predictions but cannot inspect architectures or parameters. This setting matters because operational constraints and legal restrictions may favor trading and valuing models over accessing or valuing their underlying training data.

The proposed valuation method uses a Dirichlet abstraction of model predictions. This supplies a representation through which the authors construct their equitable model valuation approach using black-box access. The contribution focuses on assigning values from observable predictive behavior, making it applicable to models whose internal details remain undisclosed.

To handle larger marketplaces, the authors use a Lipschitz continuity property of model Shapley to design a learning method that predicts valuation scores for many vendors’ models, with 150 models given as an example. They empirically validate the approach across real-world datasets and heterogeneous model types. The work thus addresses both the definition of model value and the scalability of estimating that value across a collection of different models.
neurips-2023-model-shapley-equitable-mod.tldr: Model Shapley values pretrained models using only their predictions and learns to estimate those values across larger marketplaces.

paragraphs: The paper studies Gaussian mean estimation and linear regression with Gaussian covariates under Huber contamination. Its goal is to achieve optimal estimation error while using nearly optimal amounts of data and almost linear computation. These requirements address statistical accuracy and computational feasibility together.

For mean estimation in d dimensions and a sufficiently small contamination parameter epsilon, the algorithm uses roughly d divided by epsilon squared samples, up to logarithmic factors, and achieves Euclidean error proportional to epsilon. The authors obtain the same sample scaling and error order for robust linear regression, also with almost linear runtime.

For mean estimation, the result improves on earlier methods that achieved the error guarantee with polynomially worse sample and time requirements. For regression, the authors identify their method as the first with polynomial sample and time complexity to attain the optimal error, resolving an open question. Their technical contribution is a methodology for almost-linear-time multidirectional filtering, which they suggest may be useful beyond these two Gaussian estimation problems.
neurips-2023-near-optimal-algorithms-for.tldr: New robust Gaussian estimation algorithms combine optimal error with near-optimal sample requirements and almost linear runtime.

paragraphs: The paper explores whether models pretrained on language or images can provide a common foundation for time-series analysis. Tasks such as forecasting, classification, and anomaly detection often use separate specialized approaches. The authors identify the shortage of large-scale time-series training data as a barrier to developing a unified pretrained model.

Their Frozen Pretrained Transformer reuses models trained on billions of tokens while keeping the self-attention and feedforward layers in the residual blocks unchanged. They then evaluate the approach through fine-tuning across major time-series task types. This uses representations learned in other domains as a starting point for temporal data analysis.

The reported results are comparable to or better than the state of the art across the main task categories evaluated. The authors also find theoretical and empirical similarities between self-attention and principal component analysis. That observation offers an explanation for how pretrained Transformers can bridge domains, helping connect the practical transfer results with a proposed account of the shared processing behavior.
neurips-2023-one-fits-all-power-general-.tldr: Frozen language and vision Transformers transfer successfully to major time-series tasks, with attention behavior linked to principal component analysis.

paragraphs: Meta-reinforcement learning aims to help agents generalize across tasks, but existing methods often struggle when tasks differ beyond parametric variations. Subtask Decomposition and Virtual Training addresses this by representing each non-parametric task as a collection of elementary subtasks. The resulting decomposition supplies a way to parameterize otherwise difficult task variation.

The approach uses a Gaussian mixture variational autoencoder to meta-learn how tasks should be decomposed. Shared subtasks enable reuse of policies learned across different tasks. A virtual training procedure then creates hypothetical combinations of subtasks, providing additional compositions through which the agent can prepare for combinations it has not previously encountered.

The authors report significant performance improvements on the Meta-World ML-10 and ML-45 benchmarks, surpassing current state-of-the-art techniques in their evaluation. These results support the use of learned task composition as a basis for generalization. The method’s central contribution is to connect reusable elementary policies with training on new combinations, extending the kinds of task variation that meta-learning can address.
neurips-2023-parameterizing-non-parametr.tldr: SDVT learns reusable subtasks and trains on hypothetical combinations to improve meta-reinforcement learning across non-parametric task variations.

paragraphs: DiffPreT pretrains a protein encoder by learning from sequences and structures jointly. The motivation is that focusing on either source alone leaves their relationship unexplored. Modeling both can integrate information about sequence co-evolution with structural characteristics, supporting a more comprehensive representation for protein understanding.

The training task asks the encoder to recover native sequences and structures from perturbed versions along a joint diffusion trajectory. SiamDiff extends this idea to account for the different conformations a protein can take. It maximizes mutual information between representations of diffusion trajectories from structurally correlated conformers, encouraging the encoder to capture their relationship.

The authors evaluate both methods on structure-based protein understanding tasks at atom and residue levels. DiffPreT is consistently competitive across the tasks, while SiamDiff achieves a new state of the art when results are summarized by mean rank across tasks. That aggregate finding supports explicitly modeling conformational relationships alongside sequence and structure; it does not imply that SiamDiff ranks first on every individual task.
neurips-2023-pre-training-protein-encode.tldr: DiffPreT and SiamDiff use joint sequence-structure denoising and related protein conformations to learn stronger protein representations.

paragraphs: Progressive ensemble distillation starts with a large pretrained teacher and seeks to represent it through an ensemble of smaller student models with low inference costs. The resulting collection supports flexible choices between predictive accuracy and computation. This changes how distillation serves deployment: the output is a set of smaller models that can offer adjustable inference behavior.

The proposed method, B-DISTIL, builds that ensemble using a boosting procedure. Its aggregation rules allow function composition, giving the combined students an expressive way to represent the teacher. This composition is central to the approach because the ensemble must provide useful predictive performance while being assembled from small constituent models.

The authors demonstrate B-DISTIL by decomposing pretrained models across image, speech, and sensor datasets. They also provide theoretical guarantees for convergence and generalization. Together, these contributions support a route from a single large model to an ensemble designed around inference flexibility, with both empirical evaluations across data types and formal analysis of the learning procedure.
neurips-2023-progressive-ensemble-distil.tldr: B-DISTIL decomposes a large pretrained model into smaller students that offer a flexible accuracy-versus-inference-cost tradeoff.

paragraphs: Feature transformation builds new features from existing ones to improve downstream prediction. Searching over combinations of features and operations becomes difficult as expressions grow more complex. The paper addresses this expanding discrete search space by learning a continuous representation of transformation sequences and optimizing within that representation.

The framework begins with reinforcement-enhanced preparation of training examples that associate transformations with predictive accuracy. It then embeds transformation operation sequences in a continuous space. Gradients guide a search for potentially better embeddings, after which a reconstruction step converts a selected embedding back into a transformation sequence that can define new features.

This organization connects knowledge from evaluated transformations with a search procedure that operates on their learned representations. Reconstruction is the link that turns the continuous search result into an actionable feature transformation. The authors report extensive experiments and case studies supporting effectiveness and robustness. The search is intended to uncover superior candidates; the abstract does not establish that it always finds a globally optimal transformation.
neurips-2023-reinforcement-enhanced-auto.tldr: The method embeds feature transformations into a continuous space, searches with gradients, and reconstructs promising transformation expressions.

paragraphs: Distributed representations can encode several attributes together, such as a text’s topic, sentiment, and author characteristics. Concept erasure aims to remove a selected attribute while retaining as much other information as possible. KRaM approaches this task by learning a transformation of the representation space through a distance-based objective.

The objective uses a modified rate-distortion function and a distance measure defined by labels for the concept to erase. It aims to make examples with similar concept labels dissimilar in the transformed space while preserving other information. This changes the geometry associated with the unwanted concept, making the relationship between labels and representation distances central to the method.

The authors report effective erasure of categorical, continuous, and vector-valued concepts across domains. Experiments range from binary gender variables in word embeddings to vector-valued variables in GPT-3 representations. They also analyze properties of the objective and introduce an alignment score measuring similarity to the original representation space. This score addresses the accompanying goal of retaining representation information while erasing a chosen concept.
neurips-2023-robust-concept-erasure-via-.tldr: KRaM reshapes representation distances to erase labeled concepts while aiming to preserve other encoded information.

paragraphs: Federated learning must combine information from clients whose data distributions can differ. Grouping similar clients and training a model for each group can reduce conflicts, but separate models limit knowledge sharing. Clustering can also collapse when one model attracts more and more clients, effectively returning the system to a single model.

Clustered Additive Modeling combines a globally shared prediction with a cluster-specific prediction. The global model captures features common to the clusters, allowing each cluster model to concentrate on differences. Fed-CAM trains this arrangement by alternating between client clustering and model updates, with the global and cluster models learning to predict each other’s residuals.

This design allows common information to be learned across clients while retaining specialized components and updating cluster assignments during training. The authors report that adding CAM to existing clustered federated learning methods significantly improves performance without clustering collapse in the tested non-identically distributed settings. They also provide a convergence analysis of Fed-CAM, complementing the empirical evidence for the shared-plus-specialized modeling strategy.
neurips-2023-structured-federated-learni.tldr: Fed-CAM combines shared and cluster-specific models to improve heterogeneous federated learning and avoid clustering collapse in evaluated settings.

paragraphs: Bayesian optimization often continues until a fixed time or iteration budget runs out, even though deciding when to stop directly affects cost and solution quality. This paper proposes an automatic termination rule that examines already observed samples to assess whether further local search is worthwhile.

The method first attempts to identify whether the search is within a convex region. It then stops when local regret in that region falls below a predetermined threshold. To make the termination indicator more numerically stable, the authors introduce an approximation computed through a bilevel optimization problem. The stopping decision is therefore tied to a local region and an explicit tolerance.

Evaluations cover synthetic functions, reinforcement learning, and hyperparameter optimization. The authors report savings of up to approximately 80% of the computational budget, with performance degradation an order of magnitude smaller than that of comparison methods. They also find robustness to the termination criterion’s setting. These results support using past observations to guide stopping while keeping the rule’s assessment focused on local regret.
neurips-2023-why-not-looking-backward-a-.tldr: A two-step stopping rule uses observed samples and local regret to terminate Bayesian optimization early with limited empirical performance loss.
